gen-dafont-disorder-gf-noto-sans-duploya: Glowing neon-tube lettering, raw and jumbled. Disorder keeps every line one thickness with big, widely spaced glyphs, while Noto Sans Duployan stays clean and plain sans, with a wide-mouthed a and generous counters.
gen-dafont-disorder-gf-noto-sans-elbasan: Every stroke in Disorder holds the steadiness of a drawn string, with a tall lowercase and glyphs spaced well apart from each other. It earns its keep big and short, beside Noto Sans Elbasan.
gen-dafont-disorder-gf-noto-sans-elymaic: Noto Sans Elymaic is clean and modern, with open apertures and ascenders that barely rise above the x-height. And Disorder, with rope-like stems, bowls and tails, supplies the chaos while the body keeps a long stretch of text moving smoothly.
gen-dafont-disorder-gf-noto-sans-ethiopi: Noto Sans Ethiopic stands tall and sturdy, its c terminals hanging far from the bowl. Noto Sans Ethiopic gives the page its footing, while Disorder, built from one width of stroke, scatters its raw, chaotic letters above it.
gen-dafont-disorder-gf-noto-sans-georgia: Noto Sans Georgian reads modern and clean, with open curves throughout and short ascender stems on tall lowercase bodies. Over a long page it would flow easily, with Disorder's rounded-wire letters up top.
gen-dafont-disorder-gf-noto-sans-glagoli: Noto Sans Glagolitic keeps its round letters open and clear, with a tall, sturdy lowercase. Noto Sans Glagolitic is the approachable plain sans here, while Disorder's untapered, quill-free strokes bring the raw, chaotic edge.
gen-dafont-disorder-gf-noto-sans-gothic: Disorder's flat, unmodulated strokes give it a raw, chaotic bluntness, with a tall lowercase and glyphs set far apart. Noto Sans Gothic, with counters like drilled glass beads, would read smoothly over many lines.
gen-dafont-disorder-gf-noto-sans-grantha: Disorder has a smooth drawn-wire feel running through every sentence, chaotic yet raw, with a big lowercase. Noto Sans Grantha does the quieter job, its tall little letters reading without snagging on closed-up bowls.
gen-dafont-disorder-gf-noto-sans-gujarat: Noto Sans Gujarati reads clean and modern, with curved strokes that stop before turning inward and large open counters in a, e and s. Disorder handles the loud work with stout pipe-cleaner strokes, and the body handles the reading.
gen-dafont-disorder-gf-noto-sans-gunjala: Chunky, crayon-tall and jumbled, Disorder makes its joins as thick as its strokes. Noto Sans Gunjala Gondi pulls its terminals back to leave a big gap, which is the pair's sharpest quality.
